review_notes: I read the whole file and searched the SwitchChain directory for uses of Assignment and powersetCard. I did not open the definitions in PairFiberDegree. The other types are not Mathlib duplicates: GraphFiber and StateFiber are problem-specific subtypes. Assignment is the only candidate. It is used only inside this file, and nothing outside the file refers to it. I did not check how the equivalences are used downstream. The case for consolidating is moderate, because Assignment is a deliberate-looking subtype and the rest of the project may prefer it.

findings.excerpt: {T : Finset V // T ⊆ singletonSet G i j ∧ T.card = (leftSet G i j).card}
findings.problem: Assignment is a hand-rolled subtype of Finset V. It is the set of k-element subsets of a fixed finset s, with s = singletonSet G i j and k = (leftSet G i j).card. Mathlib already has this as Finset.powersetCard k s, whose coerced type is ↥(s.powersetCard k). The membership lemma Finset.mem_powersetCard states exactly the same conjunction. The file itself builds the equivalence with ↥(powersetCard …) by hand inside assignment_natCard, using local toFun and invFun built from mem_powersetCard. That is a repeated conversion. Because Assignment is a separate type, Mathlib lemmas about powersetCard (card_powersetCard, Fintype instances, sums over powersetCard) cannot be applied to it directly. The rest of the project already uses ↥(T.powersetCard 2) as the index type, for example in pairEquiv.
findings.proposed_change: Define `abbrev Assignment (G : SimpleGraph V) (i j : V) := ↥((singletonSet G i j).powersetCard (leftSet G i j).card)`. This needs a DecidableEq V instance, or `open Classical`. Keep the name Assignment. Then graphFiberEquiv needs only `Finset.mem_powersetCard.mpr` and `.mp` at its two use sites, and the local equivalence `e` in assignment_natCard disappears. That theorem then reduces to `Nat.card_eq_fintype_card, Fintype.card_coe, Finset.card_powersetCard`.
findings.benefit: Assignment becomes the Mathlib type, so Fintype and card lemmas and powersetCard sum lemmas apply directly. This removes the ad hoc equivalence and keeps the descriptive name.
